question: The nominal scale of a Lambert conformal conic chart is the:

options.text: mean scale between pole and equator
mean scale between the parallels of the secant cone

explanation: The quoted (nominal) scale of a Lambert chart applies on the standard parallels.

question: The convergence factor of a Lambert conformal conic chart is quoted as 0.78535. At what latitude on the chart is earth convergency correctly represented?
explanation: On a Lambert chart convergency is correct at the parallel of origin where n = sin lat: sin⁻¹ 0.78535 ≈ 51°45′.

question: The scale on a Lambert conformal conic chart:

options.text: is constant along a meridian of longitude.
is constant across the whole map.
varies slightly as a function of latitude and longitude.
is constant along a parallel of latitude.

explanation: Lambert scale depends only on latitude: it is constant along any parallel.

question: On a Lambert Conformal Conic chart great circles that are not meridians are:

options.text: curves concave to the parallel of origin.
curves concave to the pole of projection.
straight lines within the standard parallels.

explanation: On a Lambert chart great circles (other than meridians) are curves concave to the parallel of origin — almost straight over the area of the chart.

question: The constant of the cone of a Lamberts chart is given as 0.75. A straight line drawn from A (45° N 60° W) to C on 10° W passes through B on 28° W. The direction of the track is 055° (T) at A. The approximate rhumb line track from A to B is:
explanation: Chart convergency A→B = 32° × 0.75 = 24°. The straight line changes direction by 24°, so the rhumb line A→B ≈ initial track + half = 055 + 12 = 067°T.

question: On a Lambert conformal conic chart, with two standard parallels , the quoted scale is correct:

options.text: in the area between the standard parallels

explanation: With two standard parallels the stated scale is correct along those two parallels.

question: A straight line is plotted on a Lamberts chart from A (35° N 145° W) to B (47° N 125° W) which measures 044° T at A. What is the rhumb line track from A to B measured at B?
explanation: With n ≈ sin 41° ≈ 0.66, chart convergency over 20° d.long ≈ 13°. The straight line goes 044° → 057°; the RL is the mean ≈ 051°, and an RL has the same direction at both ends.

question: On a Lambert conformal conic chart the distance between parallels of latitude spaced the same number of degrees apart:

options.text: expands between, and reduces outside, the standard parallels.
reduces between, and expands outside, the standard parallels.
is constant between, and expands outside, the standard parallels.

explanation: Inside the standard parallels scale is contracted, outside it is expanded — so the parallel spacing reduces between and expands outside.

question: A course of 120° (T) is drawn between X (61° 30N) and Y (58° 30N) on a Lambert Conformal conic chart with a scale of 1: 1 000 000 at 60° N. The chart distance between X and Y is:
explanation: D.lat 3° = 180 NM; along a 120° track, distance = 180 / cos 60° = 360 NM = 666.7 km → 66.7 cm at 1 : 1 000 000.

question: The standard parallels of a Lamberts conical orthomorphic projection are 07° 40N and 38° 20N. The constant of the cone for this chart is:
explanation: n = sin(mean of standard parallels) = sin 23° ≈ 0.39.

question: On a Lambert chart (standard parallels 37° N and 65° N), with respect to the straight line drawn on the map the between A ( N49° W030° ) and B (N48° W040° ), the:

options.text: great circle is to the north, the rhumb line is to the south.
great circle and rhumb line are to the north.
great circle and rhumb line are to the south.
rhumb line is to the north, the great circle is to the south.

explanation: Between the standard parallels and south of the parallel of origin, the GC (concave to the parallel of origin) lies north of the straight line and the RL (concave to the pole) lies south of it.

question: On a Lambert Conformal chart the distance between meridians 5° apart along latitude 37° North is 9 cm. The scale of the chart at that parallel approximates:
On a Lamberts chart, scale is smallest at:
explanation: Scale is smallest (most contracted) at the parallel of origin, midway between the standard parallels.

question: Where on a Lamberts chart will a great circle be a perfectly straight line?
explanation: Only meridians (which are great circles) are exactly straight on a Lambert chart.

question: The constant of the cone of a Lamberts chart is given as 0.75. A straight line drawn from A (45° N 60° W) to C on 10° W passes through B on 28° W. The direction of the track is 055° (T) at A. The direction of the straight line track A to C, measured at B is:
explanation: Chart convergency A → B = 32° × 0.75 = 24°. The straight line changes direction by that amount: 055 + 24 = 079°T at B.

question: A Lambert conformal conic chart has a constant of the cone of 0.80. A straight line course drawn on this chart from A (53° N 004° W) to B is 080° at A; course at B is 092° (T). What is the longitude of B?
explanation: Chart convergency = 092 − 080 = 12° = n × d.long → d.long = 12/0.8 = 15°. 004°W + 15° = 011°E.

question: A line is drawn on a Lamberts Conformal chart which follows a parallel of latitude between 007° 20E and 003° 30E and represents 135 nm. The parallel of latitude on which the line is drawn is:
A Lamberts Conical conformal chart has standard parallels at 63N and 41N. What is the constant of the cone?
explanation: n = sin(mean of standard parallels) = sin 52° ≈ 0.788.

question: On a Lambert conformal chart the distance between two parallels of latitude having a difference of latitude = 2° , is measured to be 112 millimetres. The distance between two meridians, spaced 2° longitude, is, according to the chart 70 NM. What is the latitude in the centre of the described square?
explanation: 2° d.lat = 120 NM ↔ 112 mm. 2° d.long reads 70 NM: cos lat = 70/120 → lat ≈ 54°.

question: On a Lambert chart, chart convergency is equal to Earth convergency at:
explanation: Lambert chart convergency equals earth convergency at the parallel of origin.

question: A Lambert conformal conic chart has a constant of the cone of 0.75. The initial course of a straight line track drawn on this chart from A (40° N 050° W) to B is 043° (T) at A; course at B is 055° (T). What is the longitude of B?
explanation: Chart convergency 12° = 0.75 × d.long → d.long 16° → 050°W + 16 = 034°W.

question: On a Lambert conformal chart the distance between two parallels of latitude having a difference of latitude = 2° , is measured to be 112 millimetres. The distance between two meridians, spaced 2° longitude, is, according to the chart 70 NM. What is the scale of the chart, in the middle of the square described?
The parallels on a Lambert Conformal Conic chart are represented by:
explanation: Lambert parallels are arcs of concentric circles.

question: The angular difference, on a Lambert conformal conic chart, between the arrival and departure track is equal to:
explanation: On a Lambert chart the change in direction of a straight line between departure and arrival equals the chart (map) convergence.

question: A straight line on a Lambert Conformal Projection chart for normal flight planning purposes:

options.text: can only be a parallel of latitude.

explanation: A straight line on a Lambert chart is approximately a great circle.

question: The two standard parallels of a conical Lambert projection are at N10° 40 and N41° 20. The cone constant of this chart is approximately:

On a Lamberts chart a straight line track crosses a meridian with a direction of 043° T and a second meridian with a direction of 055° T. If the constant of the cone is 0.75 the difference in longitude between the meridians is:
explanation: Chart convergence 12° = 0.75 × d.long → d.long = 16°.

question: The constant of the cone, on a Lambert chart where the convergence angle between longitudes 010° E and 030° W is 30° , is:
explanation: n = chart convergence/d.long = 30/40 = 0.75.
